lesson.title: Return With Time
lesson.hook: Two connected choices. Watch what your first shot creates.
lesson.liveIntro: This serve arrives more slowly. Watch where it bounces and where you are standing.

tt1A.name: What has your return created?
tt1A.sit: Their reply is deep and wide to your backhand. The return gave them time.
opts: Use controlled depth into the open side
Lift through the middle and recover

lines.A: The open side is tempting, but your wide contact makes it demanding.
lines.B: You reset with margin from a pressured contact. Keep recovering.

tt1A.take: Pressure comes from the serve you receive, not its first-or-second label.
tt1A.payoff: Pressure comes from the serve you receive, not its first-or-second label.
tt1A.principle: Use the time. Apply pressure, then read what comes back.
tt1A.why: More preparation time and an organised contact make controlled return pressure available. Depth changes where the server plays next. If the next ball pushes you wide, reset; if it sits shorter, pressure is an option. A safe reset remains defensible.

tt1B.name: What has your return created?
tt1B.sit: Their reply lands shorter. You can move forward and organise the forehand.
opts: Use controlled depth into the open side
Lift through the middle and recover

lines.A: You use the shorter reply without aiming for the line. The point continues.
lines.B: A sound reset. This shorter ball also offered controlled pressure.

tt1.name: What can you do with the time available?
tt1.sit: This serve arrives more slowly. Watch where it bounces and where you are standing.
tt1.q: What can you do with the time available?
opts: Guide the return short through the middle
Use controlled depth into the backhand side

lines.A: The short return lets them move in. Now read the pressure they create.
lines.B: You use your time to move them back and across. Watch their reply.

pro.label: Serena · Still looking for her chance
pro.moment: Facing a fifth match point against Ajla Tomljanović at the 2022 US Open, Serena found an opportunity inside the pressure: a soft second serve. She stepped into an inside-out forehand return winner. Even with the match on the line, she recognised a ball she could attack.
pro.read: Your next point: this slower serve gives you time to prepare. Use that time for a purposeful return, then read the reply; you do not need Serena’s winner.
pro.src: Sean Gregory · TIME · US Open, September 2022

drill.name: Two-ball read
drill.how: Have a partner vary serve pace without announcing it. Return to a large target and call the depth of the next ball before playing it.
